summary.intent: Work through the NEXT-WORK plan for the callisto repo toward v1: fix release bugs, close test and docs gaps, do refactors, and land the resulting PRs cleanly, including migrating schemars and stacking or rebasing PRs to avoid conflicts.
summary.outcome: Opened and got merged a large batch of PRs: SYS-RETRY fix, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init/derive refactors, SYS-NAPI, range hard-stop, dist-tag, canonical report ids, ecosystem-qualified --package, edition 2024, schemars 1.x, fuzz targets and unwrap denial. The A2 HEAD-binding fix is committed locally with CI green, but not yet pushed or opened as a PR.

repo: Local tracking plans such as NEXT-WORK.md must never go in a commit or PR. They live at .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md, excluded via .git/info/exclude.
`just ci` is the gate, run per worktree. The wrapper task's exit code is unreliable, so read the log's own `exit=` line.
docs/errors.md has a total-code count that every PR adding an E-code bumps, so such PRs conflict with each other and need rebasing after each merge.
Tests that pass bare package names fail once `--package` requires `ecosystem/name` (E317). Newly merged tests must be re-qualified when rebasing.
Generated workflow templates are .tmpl files under crates/callisto-graph/src/templates, with insta snapshots and real-jq black-box tests. macOS bash lacks `mapfile`, so templates need portable loops.
Release harness fakes (gh, cargo, registry) can hide bugs, so the plan wants proof with the real tool where possible.
Edition 2024 migration needed temp-env for env mutation, a pinned style edition, and clippy let-chain autofixes.
Native PR stacks are linked with `gh stack link`.
Commits are signed, and AGENTS.md says no session links in commits or PRs.
Mutation testing (breaking the source temporarily) is used to prove new tests can fail.

code.finding: Local release route selection: a package tagged at HEAD is now observed across registry, tag and GitHub release rather than treated as released. A preview with no origin push URL must skip registry observation.
Tag type detection must read only the object type, because multi-paragraph or signed tag messages made the old for-each-ref parsing error.
New module for A2: detects a published version on a later commit so release refuses instead of binding to HEAD.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, then fix, and mutate the source to confirm tests catch regressions.
Check pairwise merge conflicts across open PR branches before opening a batch, and stack PRs that touch the same files.
Sandbox blocks cargo registry writes, network tests, GPG signing and gh TLS. Those steps need to run outside the sandbox or the sandbox needs widening via /sandbox.
The command guard rejects inline scripts and heredocs, so write scripts to files and use the Edit tool.
Push explicitly to the PR branch when the local branch name differs from the remote's.
Get an independent agent review of risky PRs such as #202.

friction: Wrongly opened PR #201 for a local tracking plan, which the user objected to and which required closing it.
Sandbox restrictions repeatedly blocked crate downloads, signed commits, gh TLS, inline scripts and some tests, forcing out-of-sandbox retries.
Merge conflicts across parallel PRs on docs/errors.md, status.rs and the edition PR, because overlap wasn't checked up front.
PR #281 failed hosted CI because bare package specs in newly merged tests hit E317.
Task-notification exit codes misleadingly showed 0 when the underlying CI had failed (exit=1, 100, 101).
Background sessions could not edit the shared checkout plan file.
A plain `git push` silently did nothing because of a branch name mismatch.
Dependabot #275 failed on the schemars major bump until the migration merged.
open_items: Push and open the PR for the A2 HEAD-binding fix, which is committed with CI green.
A2 design call on false refusals for the local route, written up in the plan.
Release plumbing: floating v1 action tag, Intel-mac and aarch64-linux binaries, T08 selection, and T12 with scratch-registry credentials.
W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI.
W0 branch cleanup: stale local and remote branches, deletion pending the user's per-branch call.
D01 decision blocks SYS-MATURIN and W9. W10 needs decisions on target-declaration graph edges and Python dev-group cascade.
Python dev-table warning was dropped because it would be noisy for uv setups.
Fuzz targets are compile-checked only and haven't run under libFuzzer. E176 was never reproduced against a real registry.
OIDC trusted publishing is post-1.0. The user still needs to accept ADR 12 and cut 0.12.0 (#248).
Leftover branch docs/next-work-plan still exists on the remote and in a locked worktree.
